category_title: Students with ASD who initially engage through physical/sensory exploration and develop joint attention
student_description: Student A engages with novel stimuli through intense, multi-sensory physical exploration, sometimes fixating on parts of living beings rather than the whole. He is prone to sudden disengagement ('having had enough') and retreats to sensory behaviors when overwhelmed or pressured. He uniquely requires a gentle, facilitative approach that maximizes his control and strictly avoids direct questions or instructions.

criteria.rationale: Direct questions and instructions trigger this student to switch off and retreat to sensory behaviors.
criteria.check: The tutor uses comments, observations, or shared affect (e.g., laughing, praising) to engage the student, explicitly avoiding direct questions or commands.

criteria.rationale: The student tends to fixate intensely on specific parts of living beings, requiring gentle redirection to understand the whole being.
criteria.check: If the student fixates intensely on a specific physical part of an object or being, the tutor gently intervenes to redirect their attention to the whole entity.

criteria.rationale: The student struggles with direct communication but can connect when a shared interest is used as a mediator.
criteria.check: The tutor uses the student's focus on the object/animal as a bridge to build joint attention with the student (e.g., by joining the play or suggesting a turn-taking game) rather than just directing the student-animal interaction.

criteria.rationale: The student is prone to sudden disengagement or over-arousal when they have 'had enough' and cannot be forced back into a task.
criteria.check: When the student shows signs of sudden disengagement or over-arousal, the tutor reduces pressure and facilitates regulation rather than prompting them to return to the task.
